pois.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
pois.description: The surviving market after the 2018 relocation to Toyosu. 400+ stalls selling fresh seafood, tamagoyaki, pickles, and kitchenware. Opens 5am–2pm — arrive by 7am for the best sushi breakfast.

pois.name: Tsukiji Inner Market (Toyosu)
pois.description: The wholesale market relocated to Toyosu in 2018. View the famous tuna auctions from the observation deck (reservation required). The market hall is a cathedral of seafood — 500+ dealers under one roof.

pois.name: Sushi Restaurant Row
pois.description: Concentration of sushi restaurants in the outer market. Standouts: Sushi Dai (3hr queue, worth it), Sushi Daiwa (better queue, same quality), and Kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt) for budget options.

pois.name: Tsukiji Station
pois.description: Hibiya Line station (exit 1 for outer market). 5 minutes from Ginza, 15 from Tokyo Station. The station walls are decorated with fish mosaics — a hint of what awaits above ground.

pois.name: Tsukiji Market History
pois.description: The market operated from 1935–2018 — 83 years as Tokyo's seafood heart. At its peak, 2,500 tons of fish passed through daily. The iconic neon sign and clock tower were preserved as monuments.

pois.name: Tsukiji Business Center
pois.description: Modern office towers built on the former market site. The 120m Tsukiji Tower (2023) is the new landmark. The area is transforming from fish market to financial district — Tokyo's 'new Ginza'.
